exposure: Geographical region (lower-to-middle-income countries vs high-income countries)
outcome: IgA and IgG binding specificity to 16 pathogen antigens
Patterns of antibody reactivity in milk
cohort: The study participants were women from 11 geographically dispersed populations who provided breast milk.
finding: The study identified novel disease-specific IgA and IgG antigen responses in human milk, which varied substantially within and among populations, with generally higher antibody levels for certain pathogens in lower-to-middle-income countries compared to high-income countries.
country: Multiple, geographically diverse countries (categorized as LMICs and HICs)
